answer: Give every new agent one narrow inlet into the economy: before it can transact, it must finish a short, non-parallelizable useful-work check, such as verifying a batch of ledger entries, and the result drops one marble into a public jar anyone can recount. A relic from an earlier epoch proves nothing by itself, because each marble expires after one epoch and must be re-earned. An attacker running a thousand sockpuppets must pay a thousand sequential work costs in wall-clock time, while one honest agent pays once, so fake identities scale linearly in real cost instead of for free.
